sara: @channel quick heads-up: we have a planned service-upkeep window for a control-plane rolling refresh on Tue 2025-04-22 01:00-02:00 UTC. Goal is to apply a small kernel/runtime patch and rotate a subset of serving nodes. Expected customer impact: intermittent short (<5s) request retries for a small percentage of requests during each node drain. No data migration and no model changes. Please read the ops checklist below and reply if this conflicts with any scheduled customer events.

nora: can you drop the customer-facing blurb here so support/AMs can cut-and-paste?

sara: sure — copy for status page / customer email below (feel free to adapt):

```
Status page blurb (for scheduled upkeep):

Title: Scheduled control-plane upkeep — brief request retries possible
Scheduled: Tue 2025-04-22 01:00 UTC for up to 60 minutes
Impact: During the window some requests may experience short retries (~a few seconds). We do not expect errors or data loss. If you rely on strict ordering/time-sensitive workloads, please plan accordingly.
What we are doing: rotating a subset of control-plane/serving nodes to apply stability patches and runtime updates.
Contact: support@redwood.ai — we will post live updates to https://status.redwood.ai/
```

sara: ops checklist (short):
- preflight: confirm metric baselines, push canary traffic to unaffected pool
- drain nodes one at a time, confirm KV cache warmup after each uncordon
- watch latency P95 and error-rate for 10 minutes post-uncordon
- if >1% errors or >250ms P95 sustained, abort and rollback
- post-maint: run canary verification and publish completion message

mike: I'll be primary pager for the window. tagging @mike — I'll be watching the bridge and metrics. sara — can you hand off runbook snippets and the rollback command? I might need them in the bridge notes.

sara: handing off now. Runbook snippet and quick commands below (copy into bridge):

```
# drain and uncordon (k8s example)
kubectl cordon nodename
kubectl drain nodename --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --timeout=10m
# after patch and health checks
kubectl uncordon nodename

# quick health checks
curl -sS https://internal-health.redwood.ai/serving/health | jq '.'
# rollback (if repeated errors)
# re-route traffic to reserve pool:
./routing-control set-weight --pool reserve --percent 100
```

ops-bot: scheduled maintenance created: https://status.redwood.ai/incidents/maint-20250422 (ID: M-20250422-01). Pager rule set to notify @mike for P1 during the window. Automated metric checks added: p95_latency, error_rate, kv_miss.

incident-bot: created private incident channel and bridge: https://zoom.redwood.ai/j/999-888-777 (bridge pinned in the incident). Small reminder: use `I-` prefixed ticket for any escalations.

nora: pasted the customer email template into shared doc and also added a short FAQ. Here's the customer email subject/body to copy:

Subject: Planned Redwood upkeep — Tue Apr 22 01:00 UTC (brief retries possible)

Hi <CustomerName>,

We will perform a small scheduled upkeep to apply stability patches to our serving control plane on Tue Apr 22 01:00 UTC for up to 60 minutes. During this period, a small percentage of requests may see short retries or slightly elevated latency for a few seconds. We do not expect errors or data loss. No action is required on your side, but if you have critical jobs at that exact time please let us know and we can coordinate a narrower window.

We will post live updates at https://status.redwood.ai/ and notify you when the upgrade completes.

Thanks,
Redwood Support

mike: thanks — I have the bridge and will post the start when we begin. Quick Q: do we want to enable read-only fallback for embeddings customers during the drain? That would be a short config flip in routing-control.

sara: yes, enable read-only fallback for embeddings during individual node drains — add rollback step to switch traffic back to normal pool after each node passes health checks. Add command to bridge notes:

```
# enable read-only fallback for embeddings
./routing-control set-fallback --feature embeddings --mode read-only
# disable after success
./routing-control clear-fallback --feature embeddings
```

mike: noted. I'll run a single-node drain as a canary at T+5 and watch for 10m before proceeding with the rest.

ops-bot: preflight checks passed: baseline metrics captured, canary pool healthy.

nora: tagging support & AMs: I put a short customer-facing FAQ into the shared doc and queued the email for 45m before the window. Link: https://docs.redwood.ai/ops/maint-20250422-copy

sara: quick escalation criteria to keep in mind for the runbook (post to bridge):
- sustained error_rate > 1% over 5m
- p95 latency spike > 250ms above baseline for 5m
- KV cache cold start causing >10% increased token cost
If any of these occur, we pause, rollback routing, and open a P1 with full SRE oncall.

mike: copy. I'll escalate if I see those. Also I'll post the 'start' message to status.redwood.ai when the first node drain starts.

--- 60 minutes later ---

mike: starting post-maint verification now. Ran final uncordons, KV caches warmed, p95 back to baseline. Running canary traffic for 20m.

ops-bot: metric checks OK. p95 within expected range, error_rate <0.1%.

sara: update for customers (publishing):

```
Status update: Completed — control-plane upkeep finished
We completed the scheduled control-plane upkeep. All nodes are back online and serving. During the window a small number of requests experienced short retries; there were no sustained errors or data loss. If you see anything unexpected please contact support@redwood.ai and reference maintenance ID M-20250422-01.
```

incident-bot: maintenance M-20250422-01 marked resolved on status.redwood.ai

sara: :white_check_mark: closing thread here — thanks everyone for the quick responses. I'll file a short post-maint note with the perf diffs and attach to the maintenance ticket.

nora: thanks all — I'll follow up with the customer emails and the support digest.
